target: The final Java-promoted perfect-aim fighter at the league's stopping check.
reason_for_opponent: This archived retreating opponent produced enough W-tap acquisitions for continuation measurement in earlier development.
clock: scheduled real Java on two stock headless clients and the dedicated server
comparison: Each opening and seat uses plain W-tap through three consecutive unanswered fresh hits after the defender starts pressing. The two continuations are the champion and W-tap. Endpoints are evaluated under the same rule in both arms.
measurement: Report opening and branch qualification, hit-to-hit cycles, remaining fresh hits, remaining time, accepted returns including damage upgrades, censoring, and the inactivity-qualified version. Report later five- and ten-hit survivor landmarks separately from the common input at three. Bin by added RTT, opening and seat. Use measured branch HP, distance, ground state and first assigned-policy input to characterize native repeat comparability. Tournament win rate remains a distinct result.
scope: These seeds are reserved before any fight on them is examined. The league cannot train or promote on these continuations. Native repeats share the acquisition protocol; they are independent processes of play with observed initial-state records. Exact common-state forks are a separate simulator test.
